title: Opaque Context Resilience Validator & SDK Gating
creator: Lena Park
description:
Background: We continue to see a small but measurable class of trace gaps originating from SDKs deployed in proxy/edge environments where intermediate gateways strip or rewrite proprietary context headers. These gaps surface as missing parent spans, incorrectly attributed latency, or duplicated request entries in the console. Past mitigations (best-effort header fallbacks and sampling alignment) reduced volume but did not fully address intermittent, lossy propagation scenarios on mobile/edge customers.

Goal: Implement a lightweight validator (Opaque Context Resilience Validator) inside our SDKs and middleware that can: (1) detect evidence of lossy/opaque propagation at request time without adding significant overhead, (2) emit a compact, privacy-preserving provenance beacon when gaps are detected, and (3) gate richer recovery heuristics behind a per-tenant opt-in to preserve legacy behavior. The validator should be zero-change for customers who do not opt into recovery gating.

Success criteria:
- Validator executes in <200ns p50 on Node and <300ns p50 on Python SDK for the common hot path (no-op when propagation is healthy).
- Detects at least 90% of parent-span loss cases in our replayed test corpus without increasing false positives by >1%.
- When recovery gating is enabled for a tenant, end-to-end parentage recovery attempts must not increase average tail latency for synchronous requests by more than 5%.
- All emitted provenance beacons must be opt-out at tenant level and redact PII; redact policy documented and reviewed.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Detection heuristic: combine a compact 64-bit fingerprint of incoming headers + sequence-of-hop TTL heuristic + KV-cache miss pattern. This avoids relying on a single header name and is more robust to header rewriting.
- Recovery gating: first-class opt-in toggles in console + SDK startup flag. Recovery attempts will be best-effort and bounded (max 2 additional async probes per request) to avoid amplification and cost spikes.
- Privacy: beacons contain only anonymized fingerprints, timestamps, and non-identifying sampling buckets. No body or token material will ever be included. Legal/Privacy signoff required.
- Backwards compatibility: SDKs will default to validator-only mode (no recovery probes) to avoid surprising behavior for existing customers.

Implementation plan:
1) Spec validator API and lightweight fingerprint function, add unit tests and bench harness. (ENG owner: Amit)
2) Implement validator in Node + Python SDKs, expose opt-in config and per-tenant flag resolver.
3) Wire beacon ingestion pipeline into observability backend as a new metrics stream + sparse log index.
4) Add console toggle and per-route visibility + rollout experiment.
5) Run a replay test against the existing loss corpus and a 2-week canary with a small cohort of low-traffic tenants.

Risks and mitigations:
- False positives causing noisy beacons: mitigate by conservative sampling and a short debounce window before emitting.
- Cost of recovery probes under load: bound probes, add rate limiter and tenant-level throttle.
- Legal/privacy concerns: block until Legal reviews; feature off by default.

Related artifacts:
- Spec doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OBS/pages/OPAQUE-VALIDATOR-SPEC (draft)
- Bench harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/obs-bench/tree/opaque-validator
- Initial design PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-node/pull/6789
comments: 2026-03-01 Lena Park: Initial triage — capturing frequent trace loss patterns and proposing a small-footprint validator. Decided to prioritize privacy-preserving beacons and opt-in recovery gating.
2026-03-03 Amit Kapoor: Prototype of 64-bit fingerprint function submitted. Microbench shows ~120ns p50 on Node for compute-only. Pushed PR to bench harness.
2026-03-05 Design review (Priya Mehta): Asked for clearer UX copy in console (opt-in language) and a short FAQ for customers. Also requested a data retention limit for beacons.
2026-03-06 Security review kickoff (Tariq Hussein): flagged the need for a privacy signoff and recommended we store beacons in a separate encrypted store. Added as blocker for canary.

2026-03-08 Amit Kapoor: Node SDK implementation ready for internal review — added feature flag 'opaqueValidator.enabled' and tenant resolver hook. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-node/pull/6791
2026-03-10 QA (Rina Alvarez): Replay tests against the loss corpus completed — validator detected 92% of cases, FP rate ~0.7%. Need to validate Python numbers next.
2026-03-12 Amit Kapoor: Python SDK port completed. Bench results: ~260ns p50. Opened intake ticket for beacon ingestion pipeline (ENG-251223).
2026-03-13 Lena Park: Removed blocker tag after Legal confirmed allowable beacon fields (signed off with retention limit 30 days). Preparing 2-week canary plan targeting 10 low-traffic customers.
2026-03-13 Amit Kapoor: Added brief rollout playbook and rollback conditions to PR description. Playbook includes rate limits, monitoring dashboards, and a kill-switch via tenant flag.
(Upcoming) 2026-03-18 Product review: finalize console copy and canary cohort. Follow-ups: add telemetry for recovery probe success rate and any latency regressions.
